newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australian major banks a 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australian major banks a 'buy'.

text.p: Stockbrokers J.B. Were & Son said on Wednesday it still has a 'hold' recommendation on National Australia Bank Ltd and 'buys' on Westpac Banking Corp and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group.
Hunter's report on the banks were written before National Australia Bank's (NAB) first quarter result released last week.
NAB reported a net profit of A$582 million in the three months ended December 31, 1996 up from A$513 million a year ago.
"The recommendations are still the same, but I have upgraded my forecasts for NAB," Hunter told Reuters.
NAB reported a net profit of A$2.099 billion for 1995/96.

Hunter forecasts NAB to report a net profit of A$2.3 billion in the year to September 30, 1997 and A$2.5 billion in 1997/98, up from previous forecasts of A$2.220 billion and A$2.415 billion respectively.
Hunter also raised his dividend estimates for NAB to 94 cents a share for the 1997/98 year and 102 cents for 1997/98, up from previous estimates of 90 and 98 cents a share respectively.
On ANZ, Hunter said: "A better than expected 1996 result and increased dividend will maintain the interest in ANZ with probable rising consensus earnings momentum in the near term."
Hunter said he had upgraded the bank's earnings by seven percent for 1997 and six percent for 1998.
Hunter forecast ANZ to report a net profit of A$1.15 billion in the 1996/97 (October-September) year and A$1.27 billion in 1997/98, compared with A$1.12 billion in 1995/96.
On Westpac, Hunter said the Sydney-based bank had the strongest short term earnings growth in the banking sector.

"Forecast earnings growth is the strongest in the banking sector in the next two years, aided by recent acquisitions and share buybacks," he said. "Further regional bank acquisitions are likely, with the Victorian market a priority."
Hunter forecasts Westpac to post a net profit of A$1.13 billion in 1996/97 and A$1.25 billion in 1997/98. Westpac reported a 19.5 percent rise in net profit to A$1.13 billion in 1995/96.
NAB shares closed four cents lower at A$15.67, Westpac was 17 cents up at A$7.51 and ANZ shares were three cents up at A$8.06.
At the time of Hunter writing the report, NAB shares were at A$14.74, Westpac were A$7.20 and ANZ were A$8.04.
